top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on the common criteria. From public knowledge of Blinding, the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy, and of Solenoid, he has a hard-to-mistake voice: dense, patterned prose in which memory, the body, dream and cosmology are built into one imaginative system. The formal ambition lies in the architecture of very large books, which supports an oeuvre claim and not a single-book claim. The citation should credit the prose project and its cumulative architecture, with the poetry named only as origin, since that is the part I can defend most concretely. My preference is provisional. I have not read the works and cannot verify them independently. I cannot judge how much of the Romanian density and rhythm survives translation. Whether the later long volumes deepen the project or only restate its motifs is unresolved, and expert readers could change my view. The unanimous opening ranking is not evidence of merit and I have not counted it. The slate offers only P001 or no award, and nothing in the supplied evidence is strong enough to prefer no award over a laureate, so P000 is ranked second.
